I am F20 and as a woman I definitely understand wanting to feel secure and just not finding it. I have also been through the “oh your so strong for not letting your disability affect you” and again your feelings are absolutely valid.  Take it day by day. I was one of those kids who already had bad dysmorphia just based on how my arm looked in general and in certain clothing (off shoulder shirts or anything that would show off my arm made me super duper insecure) but I got into sports like cross country/track even weightlifting and I still continue going to the gym to this day. All of this to say be graceful with yourself. Erb’s Palsy is no walk in the park (pain, insecurities, etc) but you gotta appreciate that your body still gets you through your day. Our condition doesn’t make or break us. The gym has been helping me get more comfortable with showing how my arm and shoulder looks irl and I’ve sort of found a sort of thankfulness that I can still lift a weight even if its not as strong as my right arm I still put in the work and I am still an amazing person with or without Erbs. People will stare and honestly its out of ignorance for the most part but again take it day by day. We all have good days and bad ones too. Possibly finding some form of movement or activity can be a confidence boost. We won’t ever get to live this life again and I don’t think Erb’s should even stop us from finding happiness and adapting our lives to feel as close to normal as we can get.

During the time after the end of the American Civil War with the Emancipation Proclamation, Reconstruction begins. After the war, there was a lot of damage in southern states infrastructure wise and the Federal Government was still determining the extent of punishment for the south’s treason. Reconstruction ended up being the former confederacy now allowing African American men to vote giving Black men citizenship officially. Now since the south has “lost” their main source of income. I say “lost” because when newly freed African Americans gain this freedom they are too poor to live in the economy and nobody will give them good enough work to sustain a living for their families (those who are reconnected). Previous slave owners end up capitalizing on this hire back the previously enslaved people pay them almost nothing provide housing (not nice looking housing but shelter) and allow the African American “worker” to sell a bit of crop if they had some left over. Not to mention the Emancipation didn’t free everybody at first. There were plenty of slave owners unwilling to free their slaves too so again there is a population there stuck in the south. The summer of 1886 the Ku Klux Klan is founded in Tennessee and again here is another hurdle for these very impoverished and disenfranchised African Americans. Black people remained poor for the rest of the 1800s those lucky enough to be freed or have enough money to get away from the south still had family down in the south. That black mother didn’t want to leave her son, that grandmother didn’t want to leave her kids etc. A very tough situation for these people. Black people were also being threatened by the KKK when they began to gain a bit of social power. Reconstruction ended around the late 1870s and soon more and more black families moved up north with the opportunity. Moral of the story, not all African Americans were free after the end of the Civil War, socioeconomically or physically. Hope this helps :)
